source.reasoning_observation: For equal required energy E and ideal independent powers, reciprocal times add: 1/t_AB=1/t_A+1/t_B. The source gives a 4-minute single trial and 3-minute joint trial, hence the other alone is 12 minutes. This conclusion is conditional on the common energy endpoint and ideal loss assumption.

core1a.scientific_construction: The time to reach a common thermal endpoint is E divided by net energy accumulation rate. With two independently controlled ideal power sources A and B, their measured input powers add if their operation does not alter each other's electrical input. If loss is negligible, reciprocal endpoint times add. If a common fixed outward loss L acts once on the whole system, then 1/t_A=(P_A−L)/E, 1/t_B=(P_B−L)/E and 1/t_AB=(P_A+P_B−L)/E. Adding the two single-source net rates counts the same loss twice. The useful joint rate is their sum plus L. A changed joint-operation loss must be treated as another parameter, not silently assigned to either source. An independently measured energy requirement and electrical input make a loss hypothesis testable. Equal temperature endpoints alone do not guarantee equal energy requirements if mass, phase or capacity changes.
